character_facts: Namar commands or orders the launch of the attacking swarm.
The mini-fighter pilots wear heavy armor or enclosed combat gear while flying.
The attacking pilots are portrayed as numerous, aggressive pursuers.
characters_present: Namar (named in narration, not clearly shown in a distinct close-up)
Crew or pilots aboard larger combat craft
continuity_links: This page depicts a major escalation into open fleet combat.
The mother-coach and Purple Lancets are already in flight and become the focus of Namar's launched swarm.
dialogue_meaning: The narration explains that Namar initiates the engagement by deploying a huge swarm of small armored fighters.
The pursuing force is overwhelmingly numerous and aggressively targets a vessel called the mother-coach.
The battle is framed as visually overpowering, with explosions outshining the stars.
The Purple Lancets are under pressure from dense swarms of small attackers, likened to bloodthirsty mosquitoes.
locations: Outer space in the Harp constellation
The vicinity of the mother-coach and Purple Lancet ships during the battle
lore_facts: Namar possesses or operates a 'counterfeit planet.'
There exists a craft type called the Ostrov-class armored mini-fighter.
The setting includes a region called the Harp constellation.
There is a vessel or target referred to as the mother-coach.
There are ships or units called Purple Lancets.
The attacking force numbers 100,000 killers, according to the narration.
plot_events: Namar launches a massive attack from his counterfeit planet.
The attack consists of Ostrov-class armored mini-fighters.
A force described as 100,000 killers pursues the 'mother-coach.'
The battle intensifies in the Harp constellation, with repeated explosions lighting space.
Each Purple Lancet is shown being swarmed by numerous small hostile craft.
uncertainties: Namar is named in the narration, but no single figure on the page can be identified with certainty as Namar.
The exact visual identification of which ship is the 'mother-coach' is not fully explicit on the page.
'Purple Lancet' may refer to a class of ship or a group of vessels; the page does not define it further.
visual_summary: A two-page space-battle spread. Small top panels show a launch point on a planetary surface or installation, streams of tiny craft being deployed, and armored pilots inside cramped cockpits. Larger panels show masses of articulated mini-fighters and a huge carrier-like vessel in open space, with orange enemy craft, gunfire, explosions, and dense swarms of attackers converging around the larger ships.
